# Bookkeeping HTTP API

HTTP API of the ALICE Bookkeeping. **Internal use only.**

> Work in progress: not every resource is documented yet. Only the sections listed below exist.

## Authentication
Every request carries a JWT in the `token` **query parameter** (e.g. `GET /api/tags?token=<jwt>`).
The token's `access` claim lists the user's roles; operations marked with a role below return `403` otherwise.

## Response envelope
Successful responses are `{ "data": ... }`, with `meta.page` added on paginated endpoints.
Failed responses are `{ "errors": [ { status, title, detail?, source? } ] }`.
Note that request-validation failures are sent with **HTTP 400** while each error's `status` field says `"422"`.

## Conventions
- Filters use bracket syntax: `filter[partialText]=foo`. List-valued filters are comma separated: `filter[ids]=1,2,3`.
- Pagination uses `page[limit]` and `page[offset]`.
- Timestamps are Unix epoch **milliseconds**.
- Operations flagged `x-llm-exclude: true` change data and are **not meant for LLMs or MCP tools**; skip them when generating tools.

## Instructions for LLMs and automated agents
- **Always paginate** when an endpoint supports `page[limit]` and `page[offset]`. Never rely on the default: when `page[limit]` is omitted the server
  may return up to 5000 items, which is far too much for a model context.
- **Request at most 100 items per call** (`page[limit]=100`). This is a rule for LLMs and agents, not a server limit (the server accepts more).
- To read more, repeat the call increasing `page[offset]` by the limit until `offset` reaches `meta.page.totalCount`.
- Prefer narrowing the request with `filter[...]` parameters over reading everything and filtering afterwards.
- Endpoints that are not paginated (for example `GET /tags`) return everything: use their filters.
- Do not call operations flagged `x-llm-exclude: true`: they create, change or delete data.

## Quick start

The examples below read the server address and the JWT from the environment:

```bash
export BOOKKEEPING_URL=http://localhost:4000
export TOKEN=<your jwt>
```

`curl -g` is needed because of the `[` `]` in filter names. Note that a token in the URL ends up in shell history and server logs.

## Tags

Labels attached to logs (and runs). Each tag may notify an e-mail list and a Mattermost channel.

### `GET /tags` - List tags

Operation id: `listTags`

Returns every tag matching the filters, **not paginated**.
Returns `204 No Content` (empty body) when nothing matches, so clients must not assume a JSON body.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filter[ids]` | query | string | no | Comma separated tag ids. |
| `filter[texts]` | query | string | no | Comma separated exact tag texts. Takes precedence over `filter[partialText]`. |
| `filter[partialText]` | query | string | no | Substring match on the tag text. Ignored when `filter[texts]` is given. |
| `filter[emails]` | query | string | no | Comma separated e-mail addresses. |
| `filter[mattermosts]` | query | string | no | Comma separated Mattermost channel names. |

Responses:

- `200`: Matching tags.
- `204`: No tag matches the filters. No body.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/tags?token=$TOKEN"
```

### `POST /tags` - Create a tag (not for LLM use)

Operation id: `createTag`

**Not meant for LLM or MCP tool use** (`x-llm-exclude`).

**Required role:** `admin`

Request body (JSON):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes | Words, digits, `-` and `+` only. min length 2, max length 20, pattern `[\w\|\-+]{1,}` |
| `description` | string \| null | no | max length 100 |
| `mattermost` | string \| null | no |  |
| `email` | string \| null | no | One or more e-mail addresses, comma separated. |
| `color` | string \| null | no | pattern `^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$` |

Responses:

- `201`: The created tag.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `403`: The token lacks the role required by this operation.
- `409`: A tag with the same text already exists.

```bash
curl -g -X POST "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/tags?token=$TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text":"FOOD","description":"Food related issues","email":"cake@cern.ch,test@cern.ch","mattermost":"food-channel","color":"#ff8800"}'
```

### `GET /tags/name` - Get a tag by its text

Operation id: `getTagByName`

Looks a tag up by its exact text (case as stored). Use this when you know the label but not the id.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | query | string | yes | Exact tag text. Must be URL-encoded. |

Responses:

- `200`: The tag.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: The requested entity does not exist.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/tags/name?name=FOOD&token=$TOKEN"
```

### `PUT /tags/{tagId}` - Update a tag (not for LLM use)

Operation id: `updateTag`

Only `description`, `email`, `mattermost`, `color` and `archivedAt` can change;
the tag `text` is immutable. Set `archivedAt` to a date to archive the tag and to `null` to restore it.

**Not meant for LLM or MCP tool use** (`x-llm-exclude`).

**Required role:** `admin`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tagId` | path | integer | yes | Tag identifier. |

Request body (JSON):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | string \| null | no | max length 100 |
| `mattermost` | string \| null | no |  |
| `email` | string \| null | no | One or more e-mail addresses, comma separated. |
| `color` | string \| null | no | pattern `^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$` |
| `archivedAt` | string \| integer \| null (date-time) | no | Date to archive the tag, either an ISO 8601 date-time string or epoch milliseconds, null to restore it. |

Responses:

- `201`: The updated tag. (Status is `201`, not `200`.)
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `403`: The token lacks the role required by this operation.
- `404`: The requested entity does not exist.

```bash
curl -g -X PUT "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/tags/1?token=$TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"description":"Updated description","archivedAt":null}'
```

## Status

Health of the Bookkeeping application and of its database.

### `GET /status/database` - Get the database connection status

Operation id: `getDatabaseStatus`

Pings the database. `status.ok` is false when it cannot be reached.

Responses:

- `200`: The database host, port and status.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/status/database?token=$TOKEN"
```

### `GET /status/gui` - Get the status of the Bookkeeping application

Operation id: `getGuiStatus`

Returns the host, port and version of the running Bookkeeping server that answered the request.

Responses:

- `200`: The application host, port, version and status.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/status/gui?token=$TOKEN"
```

## Configuration

Addresses of the external services Bookkeeping links to.

### `GET /configuration` - Get the URLs of the external services

Operation id: `getConfiguration`

Returns the addresses of the services Bookkeeping links to (InfoLogger, AliECS GUI, QC GUI, ali-flp-index).
A URL is `null` when the service is not configured on this deployment.

Responses:

- `200`: The configured URLs.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/configuration?token=$TOKEN"
```

## Run types

Types of runs (e.g. calibration kinds).

### `GET /runTypes` - List run types

Operation id: `listRunTypes`

Returns the run types ordered by name, **descending**. Not paginated: there are few run types, and the result is capped to the maximum number of
items of the API (5000 by default). Pagination parameters are rejected.

Responses:

- `200`: The run types.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/runTypes?token=$TOKEN"
```

### `GET /runTypes/{runTypeId}` - Get a run type by id

Operation id: `getRunType`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `runTypeId` | path | integer | yes | Run type identifier. |

Responses:

- `200`: The run type.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: No run type has this id.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/runTypes/1?token=$TOKEN"
```

## CTP trigger counters

Counters of the central trigger processor, per run and trigger class.

### `GET /ctp-trigger-counters/{runNumber}` - List the CTP trigger counters of a run

Operation id: `listCtpTriggerCountersOfRun`

Returns the trigger counters of every trigger class recorded for the run. Not paginated.
A run without counters gives `200` with an empty list. A run that does not exist gives `404`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `runNumber` | path | integer | yes | Run number. |

Responses:

- `200`: The counters, one entry per trigger class.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: No run has this run number.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/ctp-trigger-counters/106?token=$TOKEN"
```

## Shifts

Data used to fill end-of-shift reports.

### `GET /shift-data` - Get the data of the pending shift of the calling user

Operation id: `getShiftData`

Returns what a shifter needs to write their end-of-shift (EoS) report for the **pending shift**: the current shift, or the previous one
during the 30 minutes that follow its end. Shifts last 8 hours and are Night (23h-7h), Morning (7h-15h) and Afternoon (15h-23h) in the
Geneva time zone. The shift is deduced from the current time and the calling user, not from a parameter.

`typeSpecific` depends on `shiftType`: `{ environments }` for `ECS`, `{ runs }` for `QC/PDP`, `{ runs, tagsCounters }` for `SL`, and `null`
for `SLIMOS` and `DCS`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shiftType` | query | string | yes | Kind of shift. |

Responses:

- `200`: The shift data.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: The calling user is not known to Bookkeeping.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/shift-data?shiftType=ECS&token=$TOKEN"
```

## Simulation passes

Monte Carlo simulation productions.

### `GET /simulationPasses` - List simulation passes

Operation id: `listSimulationPasses`

Returns a page of simulation passes with their statistics (number of runs, data passes and logs).
Default order is by name, descending.

List filters are repeated query parameters: `filter[ids][]=1&filter[ids][]=2`. A single value without `[]` is rejected. Filters are combined
with AND.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filter[ids][]` | query | integer | no | Keep the simulation passes with one of these ids. Repeat the parameter for several values. |
| `filter[names][]` | query | string | no | Keep the simulation passes with one of these exact names. Repeat the parameter for several values. |
| `filter[lhcPeriodIds][]` | query | integer | no | Keep the simulation passes used by data passes of one of these LHC periods. Repeat the parameter for several values. |
| `filter[dataPassIds][]` | query | integer | no | Keep the simulation passes anchored to one of these data passes. Repeat the parameter for several values. |
| `sort[id]` | query | string | no | Sort by id. |
| `sort[name]` | query | string | no | Sort by name (the default is `desc`). |
| `sort[pwg]` | query | string | no | Sort by physics working group. |
| `sort[jiraId]` | query | string | no | Sort by Jira ticket. |
| `sort[requestedEventsCount]` | query | string | no | Sort by number of requested events. |
| `sort[generatedEventsCount]` | query | string | no | Sort by number of generated events. |
| `sort[outputSize]` | query | string | no | Sort by output size. |
| `page[limit]` | query | integer | no | Maximum number of items to return. LLMs and agents must use 100 or less. |
| `page[offset]` | query | integer | no | Number of items to skip. |

Responses:

- `200`: A page of simulation passes.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/simulationPasses?page[limit]=100&token=$TOKEN"
```

### `GET /simulationPasses/{id}` - Get a simulation pass by id

Operation id: `getSimulationPass`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | integer | yes | Simulation pass identifier. |

Responses:

- `200`: The simulation pass.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: No simulation pass has this id.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/simulationPasses/1?token=$TOKEN"
```
